**Resolution Proposal – Exception `exc_tc_e01_MISSED_PUNCH_2026‑11‑03` (Date 2026‑11‑03)** | Step | Action | Owner | Target Completion | Notes | |------|--------|-------|--------------------|-------| | 1️⃣ | **Confirm the missed‑punch details** – pull the raw time‑clock logs for the employee (ID, shift schedule, expected in/out times) and verify that the punch was indeed not recorded on 2026‑11‑03. | Payroll/HR Analyst | Same business day (2026‑11‑03) | Use the time‑keeping system audit trail; note any system alerts or network outages that could have caused the gap. | | 2️⃣ | **Contact the employee** – reach out (email + phone) to the employee who missed the punch, ask for a brief written statement confirming the actual start/end times for that day and any extenuating circumstances (e.g., badge malfunction, emergency). | HR Business Partner | Within 4 hours of step 1 | Keep the communication logged in the employee’s HR file. | | 3️⃣ | **Validate the employee’s statement** – cross‑check the reported times against any supporting evidence (e.g., supervisor sign‑off, access‑door logs, project‑management timestamps, email timestamps). | Supervisor / Department Lead | Within 8 hours of step 2 | If evidence is missing, request a written attestation from the employee’s direct manager. | | 4️⃣ | **Create a corrective time entry** – manually enter the verified in/out times into the payroll system, flag the entry as “Missed Punch – Corrected” and attach the employee’s statement and supporting docs. | Payroll Specialist | By end of business day (2026‑11‑03) | Ensure the entry is approved by the employee’s manager before finalizing. | | 5️⃣ | **Update the exception log** – close `exc_tc_e01_MISSED_PUNCH_2026‑11‑03` with a resolution note that includes:
• Date of missed punch
• Corrected hours
• Reason for miss (e.g., badge reader failure)
• Preventive action taken | HR System Administrator | Same day (2026‑11‑03) | Use the standard exception‑tracking template. | | 6️⃣ | **Prevent recurrence** – if the miss was due to a technical issue (e.g., faulty badge reader, network lag), open a **Ticket #TC‑2026‑11‑03‑01** with IT to:
• Inspect/replace the hardware
• Review system logs for similar gaps
• Schedule a quick‑check audit of all readers in the affected zone. | IT Support Lead | Within 2 business days (by 2026‑11‑05) | Document the root cause and corrective actions in the IT knowledge base. | | 7️⃣ | **Communicate outcome** – send a brief summary to the employee, their manager, and payroll confirming that the missed punch has been corrected and payroll will reflect the accurate hours. | HR Business Partner | By end of next business day (2026‑11‑04) | Include a reminder of the “punch‑in/out” policy and the procedure for reporting future issues. | | 8️⃣ | **Policy reinforcement** – schedule a short refresher (email or 5‑minute huddle) for the team on proper time‑keeping practices and the importance of reporting any badge‑reader issues immediately. | HR Training Coordinator | Within 1 week (by 2026‑11‑10) | Attach the updated “Time‑Clock SOP” if any changes were made. | --- ### Quick‑Reference Checklist (for the day of the exception) 1. **Log retrieval** – Pull raw clock data. 2. **Employee outreach** – Get statement & times. 3. **Evidence cross‑check** – Verify with supervisor/other systems. 4. **Manual correction** – Enter corrected hours, attach docs. 5. **Close exception** – Document resolution in the tracking system. 6. **Root‑cause ticket** – If hardware/software, create IT ticket. 7. **Notify stakeholders** – Confirm correction with employee & payroll. 8. **Re‑educate** – Reinforce punch‑in policy. --- #### Expected Outcome - Accurate payroll for the affected employee (no under‑ or over‑payment). - Exception `exc_tc_e01_MISSED_PUNCH_2026‑11‑03` closed with a complete audit trail. - Any underlying technical issue identified and remediated, reducing the likelihood of future missed punches. Feel free to adjust the owners or timelines to match your organization’s workflow, but the core steps above should resolve the exception promptly and safeguard against recurrence.
